title: Determined Minority of New Life Presbyterian Church v. Judicial Commission of Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Items 2 and part of 5 sustained; Items 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 not sustained.
first_summary: Members of New Life Presbyterian Church challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's commission over its handling of membership dismissals and compliance with earlier Assembly directions. The General Assembly commission held that the presbytery commission exceeded BCO 57-5 membership requirements and sustained a related item in part, but did not sustain the remaining claims, including that the commission had failed to act or caused the entire conflict.

sources.supports: Identity, dispute, item-level judgments, adopted reasons, and mixed disposition.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The restored adjudication expressly identifies Complaint 6 and marks every item-level judgment adopted.
evidence_notes.dispute: The members challenged the commission's handling of dismissals and compliance with the prior Assembly's directions.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Item 2 and part of Item 5 were sustained; the remaining items were not. The decisive sustained ground was that the commission exceeded BCO 57-5 membership requirements.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The commission was criticized as unwise and as failing to enforce instructions, but those observations did not convert the corresponding items into sustained claims.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Item 5 refers internally to Item 2 of the same complaint; no separate case supplies the holding.
